description: A Python start anchor is refused at validation here; the baseline anchors the match.
descriptor: { descriptor_version: "1.0", root: { type: "object", children: { a: { type: "string", pattern: "\\Aabc" } } } }

divergence.note: docs/grammars.md §1.2 and §1.3 fix which layer reports each regex construct, and §1.2 states that the two implementations can name the same problem at different layers while the outcome (refused, named, never guessed at) does not differ. This is a documented, intentional divergence from the executed baseline under that rule (SPEC.md amendment 26), not a baseline defect.  This engine compiles \A as a literal A, so the value does not match and the dialect scan names it as outside the dialect (a `pattern` issue). The baseline treats \A as a start anchor and reports no issue. Both refuse the file eventually; docs §1.2 assigns this row to the validation `pattern` reading, which this product applies.
